name: Nobotara Apollo 11 Offline Voiceovers
description: Pre-rendered offline audio voiceover clips for Apollo 11 lunar educational simulation

clips.speaker: Neil Armstrong
clips.text: Hey, Neil Armstrong here. On July 16, 1969, we rode a Saturn V built from math, sweat, and nerve. 384,000 km to test physics where mistakes could kill. We didn’t just chase a rock in the sky; we went to learn what people can do when they dare.

clips.speaker: Neil Armstrong
clips.text: This is the Eagle’s descent stage. It helped the Lunar Module land on the Moon. The ascent stage carried me and Aldrin back into lunar orbit, while the descent stage remained behind.

clips.speaker: Scientific Voice
clips.text: The Lunar Module was built in two distinct stages. The descent stage contained the throttleable rocket engine, landing gear, and propellant tanks. Since weight was critical for orbital rendezvous, only the lightweight ascent stage lifted off to return to Earth.

clips.speaker: Neil Armstrong
clips.text: Not everything left behind became inactive. Apollo 11 astronauts placed this laser retroreflector. Scientists on Earth can send laser pulses toward it and measure the returning light to study the distance between Earth and the Moon.

clips.speaker: Scientific Voice
clips.text: Observatories in Texas, Hawaii, and France still bounce high-energy pulsed lasers off this Apollo 11 reflector. By timing the ~2.5 second round-trip with picosecond accuracy, scientists proved the Moon is drifting away at 3.8 cm per year.

clips.speaker: Neil Armstrong
clips.text: This plaque commemorates humanity’s first crewed lunar landing. It carries a message of peace from Earth. A message left behind for history to remember.

clips.speaker: Scientific Voice
clips.text: Engraved on stainless steel to withstand cosmic radiation and 300°C temperature swings: 'HERE MEN FROM THE PLANET EARTH FIRST SET FOOT UPON THE MOON JULY 1969 A.D. WE CAME IN PEACE FOR ALL MANKIND.'

clips.speaker: Neil Armstrong
clips.text: Good work, explorer. You understand why we left these pieces behind: for science, for survival, and for peace. The lunar surface keeps our story safe.

clips.speaker: Neil Armstrong
clips.text: The footprints at Tranquility Base proved that humanity could leave Earth. But our journey didn't stop at the Moon. We aimed further—beyond the planets, into interstellar space.
